topic: Texas option period: how buyers burn their walk-away window
hook: You lose 3 of your 7 walk away days.

scores.worst_problem: Slide 4's loop ("There is a wrong week for that") points at timing/scheduling, but slide 5 is about written notice — the promised payoff never arrives, so that swipe feels like a bait-and-switch.
scores.fix: Rewrite slide 4's loop so it sets up the actual next slide, e.g. "Saying it out loud fails" or "Then people blow the exit."

topic: What surprises Texas transplants (SA, Austin, DFW)
hook: The 47 day stretch nobody warns transplants about.

scores.worst_problem: A couple of loops lean on empty abstraction — "Your street decides something bigger" and "Where you buy changes more than that" tease a category without naming a stake, so they pull weaker than the concrete ones like "The bigger bill lands once yearly."
scores.fix: Rewrite the vague loops to name the noun being withheld — e.g. swap "Your street decides something bigger" for "Your street decides your school" and "Where you buy changes more than that" for "Same house, different tax bill."

topic: Texas market reality check: price cuts, inventory, concessions, and the 60 day window
hook: Four in ten Texas sellers did this last month

scores.worst_problem: The hook leans on the tired "did this" construction and, given the topic, most readers will correctly guess "cut their price" before swiping, so the gap is thinner than it looks.
scores.fix: Rewrite slide 1 to withhold something less guessable than the obvious price-cut answer — e.g. lead with the two-speed contradiction ("Same street, same month: one house sold in 9 days, one has cut twice") so the reader cannot predict the mechanism.
